agent_blueprint.description: Finds anomalies in PoroTomo DAS records that could indicate injection-induced seismicity at Brady Hot Springs, runs the detection on Aurora through PBS, and estimates the probability of a Pohang-like (Mw >= 5.5) event with the Shapiro seismogenic-index model.

metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
Headline results of the agent run in /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

RECORDS ANALYSED
- 759 records analysed, all status "ok" (manifest: 15,164 total records, selected 759 at stride 20; first 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z, last 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z). Sampled fraction of total time = 0.03314 (~3.3%); mean 2003.99 ms per record. First pass had 6 "download_failed" records (OpenSSL SSL_read errors); a retry (retry_manifest.txt / detect_retry_login.jsonl) recovered all 6, giving the final 759 ok.

ANOMALIES AND DAS DETECTIONS
- Anomalous records: 57 (z_threshold = 5.0; anomalies.csv has 57 rows, hourly.csv sums to 57 over the 759 records).
- DAS detections: 62 events in 53 records; scaled to full time = 1870.77; b_relative (Aki MLE) = 0.9849352475487246; mc_relative = -0.8492463451632817; n_above_mc = 34.

SEISMOGENIC INDEX Sigma AND P(Mw>=5.5) PER YEAR, PER b SCENARIO (hazard_catalog_based, exactly as in summary.json; P per year at the observed rate, M>=5.5):
- b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.448901270028832;  P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.00011982478978644906 (~1.2e-4)
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.3193012700288325; P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004921548824626587 (~4.9e-3)
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.280901270028833; P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.014735103451029574 (~1.5e-2)

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (hazard_das_upper_bound, exactly as in summary.json):
- b_used = 0.9849352475487246 (source: "DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE"); Sigma = -2.698279919032152; P(Mw>=5.5)/yr at observed rate = 0.07842182774171746 (~7.8e-2).

WHICH IS CALIBRATED VS UPPER BOUND
- The CALIBRATED probabilities are the catalog-based ones (hazard_catalog_based), which use the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (GDR 859; n = 5 events, mc = -0.48, mag_max = 0.07, all ML) with assumed b-values.
- The DAS-based number (P ~ 0.078/yr) is an UPPER BOUND with UNCALIBRATED magnitudes: it treats every DAS detection as an event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude and therefore over-counts; its magnitudes are relative (mrel) DAS-derived values, not calibrated ML.

ASSUMPTIONS EACH METRIC RESTS ON (as stated in the run files)
- Catalog-based probabilities rely on a very small local catalogue (5 events) and on the assumed b-values (1.0 / 0.73 / 0.65); model form is Shapiro et al. (2021) Eq. 5, P = 1 - exp(-V * 10^(Sigma - b*M)).
- The DAS upper bound extrapolates from limited DAS-derived relative-magnitude estimates and over-counts by construction.
- Only ~3.3% of the total time was sampled (stride 20), so rare events could be missed; the 8-day analysed window sits inside a 16-day pumping period (2016-03-11 to 2016-03-27; injected 465,448 m3, extracted 505,933 m3, net -40,485 m3).
- Spearman correlations between events and injection are weak (vs net injection -0.173, vs abs change -0.030, vs injection -0.093), so causality cannot be established from this run.
- Sigma choice spans -5.45 to -2.70 across scenarios and dramatically changes the probabilities; for reference, the Sigma needed for a 1% chance of Mw>=5.5 over the observed volume is -2.17 (b=1.0), -3.65 (b=0.73), -4.09 (b=0.65) — i.e. the observed site Sigma (-5.45 to -5.28) is far below those.
- Run provenance: PBS job 9092130 (detect+hazard), detect finished in 188 s at 2026-11-15T16:00:53Z, hazard at 16:00:56Z; summary.json generated 2026-11-15T16:02:33+00:00. A reviewer note in interpretation.md flags that its own raw text contained three errors (stride interpretation, which estimate is calibrated, and the direction of the Sigma comparison) — the values reported here are taken verbatim from summary.json, not from interpretation.md's prose.
